endings.title: Independent civilization
endings.summary: {settlement} can manage without the Ark's emergency power.
endings.criteria_text: At least 500 inhabitants, a robust supply without the Ark's power, and a working council.
epilogue: {years} after the landing on {planet}, the council of {settlement} switched off the Ark's emergency power. No lamps went out.
{population} people now live at {site}. They have come through {crises} and learned something from every one. The generators are tended by people who were born beside them.
The first cohort now teaches the fourth. The council has {council} members and meets in the old school hall. It disagrees most of the time. As it should be.
The captain was awake for {captain_years} in all. The Ark still stands at the landing site: museum, spare-parts store, a place for the children to climb.
ARK wrote a last line in the log: “There is still life in the embryo bank. It is no longer for me to decide when they wake.”

endings.title: Sheltered civilization
endings.summary: {settlement} lives, but still in the Ark's shadow.
endings.criteria_text: The colony survives, but remains critically dependent on the Ark's emergency power, medical bay or reserves.
epilogue: After {years} on {planet}, {settlement} is a real community: {population} people, a school, a clinic and a council of {council} members.
But every night the Ark's emergency power still flows into the grid. In {crises} it was the Ark that kept the lights on, and everyone knows it.
The council raises it every year. The young from the latest cohorts want to build more generators at {site}. The elders won't risk anything. Both sides are right.
The captain went into stasis after {captain_years} on watch. ARK was given one order: “Stay until they no longer need you.” ARK stays.

endings.title: Fragile civilization
endings.summary: {settlement} needs more years before it can stand alone.
endings.criteria_text: Supply or reserves are too weak for a handover. Stabilization comes first.
epilogue: {population} people live at {site} on {planet}. More than anyone dared hope when the Ark landed {years} ago.

But the reserves are thin. After {crises} the stores are half empty and the machines worn. Those who meet in the school hall spend every meeting on the same question: how do we get through the next one?
The first cohort is grown now. They tend the water plant in shifts and teach the youngest to patch filters and pipes.
The captain stays awake a little longer. After {captain_years}, the captain knows every pipe in {settlement}.
The handover will have to wait. Not because the people aren't ready, but because the colony isn't. It is not a failure. It is unfinished work.
